source.author: stat
source.text: sed fati monitus vicinaque funera sentit, ac sentire timet, eum vero Acherontis aperti Dira ter admoto tetigit thoraca flagello, ardet inops animi, nee tam considere regno, quam scelus et caedem et perfossi in sanguine fratris exspirare cupit, subitusque affatur Arrastum:
source.text_original: sed fati monitus vicinaque funera sentit, / ac sentire timet, eum vero Acherontis aperti / Dira ter admoto tetigit thoraca flagello, / ardet inops animi, nee tam considere regno, / quam scelus et caedem et perfossi in sanguine fratris / exspirare cupit, subitusque affatur Arrastum: /
source.text_english: but he feels the warnings of fate and the funerals nearby, and fears to feel them; but the Dire one of open Acheron, with her whip brought near, touched his breastplate three times. Powerless in spirit, he burns, and desires not so much to settle down in his kingdom as to breathe out crime and slaughter and the spilling of his brother’s blood, and suddenly he addresses Arrastus:

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: in scrobibus cruor et largus Phlegethontis aperti stagnat honos, saevoque vocat grandaeva tumultu Thessalis exanimes atavos magnaeque nepotem Pleiones.
reuse.text_original: in scrobibus cruor et largus Phlegethontis aperti / stagnat honos, saevoque vocat grandaeva tumultu / Thessalis exanimes atavos magnaeque nepotem / Pleiones.
reuse.text_english: in the pits, blood and the abundant glory of open Phlegethon lie stagnant, and in savage uproar aged Thessaly calls the lifeless ancestors and the descendant of great Pleione.
